description:
Make the lease check inside repository mutations hold one lease lock across the session and read its targets through it, without writing.

## Background

`lock_claims_for_repository_mutation` (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs`) takes the claims lock and replays the whole claims log into a `ClaimsMutationGuard`. `claims_mutation_guard` (`commands/mod.rs`) has seven call sites (`commands/dependency.rs`, `commands/gate.rs`, `commands/issue.rs`, `commands/mod.rs`), all before the repository session opens. `refuse_foreign_leases_held` and `ensure_claim_available` (`commands/mod.rs`) read the guard through `ClaimsMutationGuard::conflicting_lease`. The lifecycle path takes a preliminary guard for a claim before prechecks run and drops it before taking the held one. `CoordinationOrderGuard::enter` refuses while a repository order guard is held (`storage/guard_order.rs`). `ClaimCoordinator::lock()` returns a `LeaseLock` with `load`, `list` and `apply`. `tests/cli_repo_workflow/lease_enforcement_tests.rs` owns the holder and other-agent outcomes across every command.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The repository-mutation guard takes one `LeaseLock` before the repository session opens, holds it across the session and reads each target only through `load`. It writes nothing and nests no second claims lock or coordination guard. A lease that is not `Lease::is_active` conflicts with nobody, and an anonymous writer conflicts with every active lease.
- [hard] REQ-02: A test in `lease_enforcement_tests.rs` shows that a lease-enforced mutation leaves the claims log unchanged.
title: The repository-mutation lease check reads through the held lease lock
